messages:
incident-bot: Incident created — us-east-1 GPU fleet reporting HEALTHY<50% and intermittent scheduling failures. Auto-failover target: eu-west-1. Please coordinate DNS failover and traffic shift.

alex: seeing app errors from customers in us-east, many 503s. health dashboard shows node drain + OOMs on p4a.

maria: confirmed, control-plane shows scheduler backpressure. Starting emergency capacity spin in eu-west-1.

devon: DNS check — our weighted Route53 record didn't flip all the way. Some resolvers still returning us-east IPs. Likely TTL/cache issue.

sam: ah — TTL was 300s for the failover alias. I lowered it to 60 at 1755001400 but propagation will be uneven.

alex: can we force any cache purge upstream? Cloudflare+Fastly need purge, but public resolvers (ISP caches, 8.8.8.8) we can't purge. Workaround is to announce new VIP and wait for TTL to expire.

networking: filing a ticket with our DNS provider to flush authoritative cache and accelerate propagation. Also pushing an immediate change: flip the Route53 routing policy to failover primary->secondary so we get deterministic responses from resolvers that consult health checks.

devon: steps I'm doing now:
```
# check what resolvers are seeing
dig +short @8.8.8.8 app.redwood.prod A
dig +short @1.1.1.1 app.redwood.prod A
# see trace from random resolvers
dig +trace app.redwood.prod
```

maria: note: load balancer in eu-west has cross-region egress costs; been warned — but for availability we accept short-term cost hit. Also adjust autoscale limits in eu-west to handle burst.

sam: quick note on TTL semantics: lowering authoritative TTL helps new lookups but does not force already cached answers to expire until their remaining TTL elapses. Many ISP caches respect TTL but some use minimum floors. Expect mixed resolver behavior for ~5-10 minutes after change.

alex: observed mixed results — tracert from us-east shows hits to eu-west for some endpoints but still us-east for others. We should communicate to product/legal if SLOs will be impacted.

networking: provider confirmed they flushed their cache for the zone at 1755001560. They also increased SOA serial.

devon: I'm toggling Route53 weights now to 0/100 (us-east/eu-west). Command I'm using:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123456 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"app.redwood.prod","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west","Weight":100,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.120.45.12"}],"TTL":60}}]}'
```

sam: also to be aware — some clients cache at application level (SDKs). We should emit a short status message to customers to flush or restart affected connections.

maria: ops note: switched canary traffic first, metrics look stable. Starting bulk shift with 10% increments every 60s.

alex: still seeing small fraction of 503s from customers hitting legacy us-east nodes. mitigation: add sticky header to route health-checks to prefer eu-west for new sessions, and set edge proxies to return 302 to eu-west landing when health fails.

devon: run this to inspect unresolved TTL from several public resolvers (psuedo-run):
```
for r in 8.8.8.8 1.1.1.1 9.9.9.9; do echo "$r -> $(dig +short @$r app.redwood.prod A | tr "\n" " ")"; done
```

networking: status update from provider: some ISP-level caches are honoring old TTL for up to ~8 minutes. We can't do more than wait; continuing to monitor.

maria: cost-control reminder — enable temporary cross-region egress alert for finance so we don't get surprised. sam, can you add a tag?

sam: done. tagged affected instances with incident-1755001234 and set an alert threshold at $5k/hr.

alex: post-incident action items (quick): document TTL default behavior, add runbook step to pre-lower TTL to 30s when doing planned failovers, add automated Route53 failover policy rather than weighted. Also better messaging for SDKs.

devon: agree — also add a quick-check script that runs dig +trace from multiple public resolvers and reports percentage still pointing to old region. Will add to infra-runbooks.

incident-bot: Incident severity reduced to SEV3 at 1755001800 — traffic shifted; residual errors <1%. Monitoring for 30m, then close. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks all — keeping this thread for postmortem notes.
